key_insight: Failures that are invisible in individual agent traces can be revealed by jointly analyzing many traces; the paper introduces scalable methods that detect rare, complex, and adversarially-hidden safety violations by reasoning across sets of trajectories.
problem_solved: Finding rare, complex, or covert safety violations that only become apparent when multiple agent traces are analyzed together—an auditing challenge made harder by large trace corpora and adversarial hiding strategies.
method: Multi-trace judges: evaluate sets of traces jointly (rather than per-trace) to expose cross-trace correlations and failure modes.
Efficient search and generation: combine targeted sampling and adversarial trace generation to surface rare or hidden violations without exhaustively enumerating traces.
Scalable scoring + interpretable counterexamples: rank candidate trace-sets by violation likelihood and return compact, human-readable counterexamples for auditors.
impact: Enables more effective pre-deployment auditing by surfacing subtle, emergent, or adversarially-concealed failures, reducing blind spots in safety evaluations and helping practitioners prioritize fixes and mitigations.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: many traces → multi-trace judge / scorer → flagged cross-trace counterexample
Heatmap or rarity chart: frequency of single-trace vs cross-trace-detected failures to show what per-trace judges miss
Graph/network view: traces as nodes with shared states/inputs highlighting emergent failure pathways across traces
Bar/line chart: detection rate and sample efficiency comparison between per-trace baselines and the proposed method
paper_title: Detecting Safety Violations Across Many Agent Traces
paper_authors: Adam Stein, Davis Brown, Hamed Hassani, Mayur Naik, Eric Wong
